title: What If a Tunguska Asteroid Exploded Over a City Today?

scenes.text: What if a Tunguska-size asteroid exploded over a city today? It would not even leave a crater.
In 1908 a rock roughly 50 meters wide blew up five to ten kilometers above Siberia.
The blast flattened an estimated 80 million trees across more than 2,000 square kilometers.
That is an area bigger than most major cities, and energy estimates run from about 4 to 15 megatons of TNT.
In 2013 the far smaller Chelyabinsk blast blew out about a million windows and injured over a thousand people.
No crater, no warning. Just a shockwave from above, which is why scientists now watch the sky.
